title: Collector Interop and SIEM Translation Guide
content:
Purpose:
This guide defines a practical, interoperable contract between Redwood evidence collectors and downstream SIEM/forensics consumers. It focuses on translation semantics, minimal canonical fields for audit, RBAC v2 enforcement hooks, and migration strategies for retiring legacy exporters. The intent is to enable diverse collectors (edge agents, sidecars, serverless samplers) to emit a consistent envelope that can be reliably mapped to multiple SIEM targets (Splunk, Elastic, Sumo Logic, Datadog) with deterministic, lossless transformations where possible.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: security engineers, collector implementers, infra engineers on evidence pipelines, SREs operating SIEM exporters, and compliance reviewers.
- Scope: collector envelope spec, canonical audit fields, recommended translation mappings for popular SIEMs, RBAC v2 enforcement integration points, operational behaviors (retries, batching, idempotency), and a phased rollout plan for migration from ad-hoc exporters.

High-level design principles:
1) Single canonical envelope: collectors emit one JSON envelope per logical control-evidence event. Downstream translators perform deterministic reformatting but should not drop provenance fields.
2) Minimal required fields: include enough metadata to prove chain-of-custody, identity, and context for compliance audits.
3) Idempotency and sequencing: every envelope must include stable ids and sequence markers to allow deduplication and replay detection.
4) RBAC-linked provenance: evidence must carry the principal and decision context so RBAC v2 audits can validate who had the power to perform the action.
5) Translator neutrality: translation layers should be stateless conversions; enrichment and policy decisions belong in upstream services or dedicated enrichers.

Canonical collector envelope (required fields):
- envelope_id: stable UUID for the evidence envelope (v4 or v7)
- generated_at: RFC3339 UTC timestamp when collector observed/created the evidence
- source: short token indicating collector type (edge-agent, sidecar, k8s-admission, audit-proxy)
- tenant_id: customer or org id (opaque string)
- control_id: canonical control identifier (e.g., 'RBAC-LOGIN-001')
- event_type: action canonicalization (login, grant, revoke, config-change, model-load, data-export)
- actor: principal object serialized as a compact string (see actor encoding below)
- actor_context: list of context labels (ip, user_agent, session_id) as k=v pairs
- resource: resource locator (type:id) describing the target of the action
- result: success | failure | partial | unknown
- evidence_blob: base64 or gzipped payload reference (may be empty if not applicable)
- signature: optional detached signature metadata (sig_type, signer_id, signature_value)
- provenance: list of upstream hops (collector-id@region, timestamp) serialized as strings
- seq_no: monotonically increasing per-source sequence integer (string-encoded to avoid JS int issues)
- sha256: hash of canonicalized evidence_blob or relevant payload for tamper detection

Actor encoding recommendation:
- compact actor string format: <principal_type>:<principal_id>[@realm][|role-binding-id]
- Examples: user:ava.nambiar@redwood | svc:ingest-worker-27 | group:security-ops|rb-1242
- Rationale: compact, search-friendly, and keeps the actor readily usable in RBAC log lookups. Full actor metadata can be placed in an optional actor_metadata field for debug/enrichment.

Audit log schema notes (compatibility):
- Keep top-level timestamp as generated_at; translators should also set an @timestamp or equivalent for SIEM if required.
- When mapping to SIEM events, preserve the envelope_id as event_id in the target and map seq_no to event.sequence for dedupe.
- Do not drop tenant_id in multi-tenant exports; use dedicated routing or index-per-tenant where supported.

SIEM translation mappings (recommended):
- Splunk (hec/raw): map as flat JSON with these key renames:
  - event_id <- envelope_id
  - _time <- generated_at
  - source_type <- source
  - tenant <- tenant_id
  - control <- control_id
  - action <- event_type
  - principal <- actor
  - res <- resource
  - outcome <- result
  - evidence_ref <- evidence_blob
  - provenance <- provenance (string array)
  - sig_hash <- sha256
- Elastic (ELK): recommended index naming: security-evidence-YYYY.MM.DD-<tenant_hash>
  - @timestamp <- generated_at
  - id <- envelope_id
  - host.source <- source
  - labels.tenant <- tenant_id
  - event.action <- event_type
  - user.principal <- actor (also populate user.name if principal_type==user)
  - related.resource <- resource
  - file.hash.sha256 <- sha256 (where evidence_blob present)
- Datadog: translate to events API with title `Evidence: <event_type>` and include envelope_id and tenant_id as tags. Keep evidence_blob out of short text fields; only include a reference URL in the body.

Translation rules and pitfalls:
- Keep provenance: never drop the provenance chain. SIEM observers (and auditors) must be able to reconstruct ingestion path.
- Avoid flattening arrays of context into comma-separated strings; keep arrays when target supports them.
- Respect size caps: translators should detect oversized evidence_blob and instead emit a signed reference (object store URL with short-lived token) plus metadata.
- Sensitive redaction: do not allow translators to decide redaction._sensitive field rules must come from a policy service. Translators should call the policy-enforcer when a field is tagged sensitive.

RBAC v2 integration points:
- Decision trace: whenever a collector or gateway enforces an RBAC decision, it must append a decision_trace field with: decision_id, policy_version, decision_time, decision_result (allow/deny), and decision_provenance (source of truth). This enables later auditors to correlate evidence to the exact authorization check.
- Role-binding IDs: collectors should record role_binding_id where relevant. RBAC audit tooling will use these ids to query the role graph.
- Read path vs write path labeling: label evidence events with required_permission scope (read:resource, write:resource) so compliance can detect privilege elevation patterns.

Operational behaviors (collectors and translators):
- Batching: collectors may batch multiple envelopes for transport, but each envelope must retain envelope_id and seq_no. Batch transports must expose per-envelope delivery status in ACKs.
- Retries: implement idempotent retry logic keyed by envelope_id. If a translator or exporter cannot process an envelope, it must return an error code that surfaces to the source system for backoff/backpressure.
- Backpressure: collectors should support a pushback header from translator/ingest to slow the emit rate (X-Ingest-Window or similar).
- Observability: emit meter events for: envelopes_accepted, envelopes_rejected, translation_errors, oversized_payloads, signature_failures. Tag metrics by source and tenant.

Example canonical envelope (single line JSON for clarity):
{"envelope_id":"d3a3f9f4-2a6b-4b6a-9c3e-1b5c7ef0a9e1","generated_at":"2025-11-02T18:42:33Z","source":"edge-agent","tenant_id":"org-7a9f","control_id":"RBAC-LOGIN-001","event_type":"login","actor":"user:ava.nambiar@redwood|rb-211","actor_context":["ip=52.44.2.13","user_agent=Mozilla/5.0"],"resource":"service:console","result":"success","evidence_blob":"","signature":"","provenance":["edge-agent-12@us-west1:2025-11-02T18:42:33Z"],"seq_no":"0000000000012","sha256":""} 

Migration and rollout plan (phases):
Phase 0 - Discovery (0-4 weeks): inventory current collectors and exporters, capture sample payloads, and identify high-volume pipelines.
Phase 1 - Reference implementation (4-10 weeks): deliver a lightweight reference collector library (python/Go) that emits the canonical envelope and a stateless translator component that demonstrates Splunk and Elastic mappings.
Phase 2 - Pilot (10-14 weeks): onboard 2 non-critical collectors and one high-volume service to the reference pipeline, validate metrics, error rates, and storage costs.
Phase 3 - Broader migration (14-28 weeks): migrate remaining collectors in waves. Provide fallbacks to legacy exporters for 30 days per wave and run parallel exports for audit verification.
Phase 4 - Enforcement and cleanup (28-40 weeks): switch off legacy exporters after audit sign-off; update runbooks and deprecate older translations.

Compatibility matrix (must test):
- Legacy HEC exporters (Splunk) -> ensure no field truncation for large provenance arrays.
- Elastic ingest pipelines -> ensure index templates accept tags.
- Cloud SIEM connectors (Datadog, Sumo) -> ensure safe reference URLs instead of large blobs.

Security considerations:
- Signatures: recommend optional detached signatures for high-sensitivity evidence. Signature header must include signer_id and algorithm. Translators must validate signatures when key material is available; otherwise mark event.signature.valid=false.
- KMS integration: evidence_blob storage references should be encrypted and signed using tenant KMS keys where applicable.
- Least-privilege exporters: translators and export runners must run with narrow IAM roles that only allow write to the target sink and read from required staging objects.

Operational runbooks (short):
- On translation error: route failing envelopes to retention queue, notify owning service, and flag incident if error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m.
- On oversized evidence: generate reference URL and emit an evidence-truncated event; create ticket to evaluate policy if truncation exceeds threshold.
- On signature failure: quarantine event and surface to security team for investigation; do not automatically drop unless policy allows.

Open questions for architecture review:
- Should we include a compact binary envelope (CBOR) as a supported transport for edge-to-ingest to reduce bandwidth? Pros: smaller payloads; Cons: less human-readable for audits during early adoption.
- Do we enforce tenant-specific index routing by default for Elastic, or allow tenant tagging only?
- What's the retention policy for provenance arrays in long-running tenants (cost vs audit value)?

Appendix: checklist for implementers:
- [ ] Emit envelope_id (UUID) and seq_no per-source
- [ ] Include actor as compact string and optional actor_metadata
- [ ] Add decision_trace when the event is the result of an RBAC check
- [ ] Use signed reference for large evidence_blob (>128 KB)
- [ ] Populate sha256 where applicable
- [ ] Wire metrics and error counters with tenant and source tags
- [ ] Validate translator behavior against reference test corpus (provided in linked_artifacts)

Contacts and ownership:
- Primary owner: Priya Nambiar (security-and-compliance)
- Implementation lead: Marco Silva (platform-engineering)
- Compliance review: Yvonne Kim (legal & compliance)

This document is intended to be a living spec. Feedback and concrete samples should be posted to the linked Jira ticket (SEC-1021) and PRs for the reference implementation repo.
